title: Shift compatibility of strict diagram scalar mates
statement: Fix a prime l, finite extensions E⊆F of Q_l with embedding i, schemes X,Y, a compactification c of X→Y, and whole-system coefficient reduction calculi S,S' over E,F on X. Let e≥1 and assume Ramification(l,E,F,i,e). Use the strict constant-coefficient towers and actual maps of [lem-pur-compact-support-strict-scalar-mate], with the canonical integer shifts of [def-pur-compact-support-scalar-shift-structures]. The proper scalar mate proper(l,E,F,i,c.g), openTensor(l,E,F,i,c.i), inverse strictScalarPull(l,E,F,i,c.g), and counit of the E tower pullback/direct-image adjunction commute with every integer shift. Their prescribed full support composite arrow(l,E,F,i,c,S,S',e,he,hepos) also commutes with these shifts in the derived category of whole strict towers. Underlying definitions are those of [lem-pur-compact-support-strict-scalar-mate], [def-pur-compact-support-scalar-shift-structures].

proof.text: The pullback/scalar identification $\lambda:p_B^*C_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{\overline X}p_A^*$ in the proper transpose is the canonical balanced identification on resolving representatives. Use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] for its K-flat computation and preservation of K-flat representatives. On those representatives both routes in its shift square send the tensor of a degree-$i$ module section with degree-zero coefficient sections to the same balanced tensor. The first-variable shift in [lem-pur-derived-tensor-additive-constraints] is $t_{r,0}$, whose factor $(-1)^{0i}$ is $1$; unsigned reassociation introduces no additional factor. Hence the shift square is an equality of chain maps, and the resolving-localization full faithfulness in that statement makes it the equality of the actual derived natural comparisons. In particular this assertion is about the specified balanced $\lambda$, not about some isomorphism between its source and target. The same calculation applies on a small ringed diagram site.

proof.text: Write $L_A=p_A^*$, $R_A=Rp_{*,A}$ and similarly for $B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift], the canonical counit has, after inserting the comparisons, $\varepsilon_{N[r]}=\varepsilon_N[r]$; this holds for all $r$, not only $1$. The defining transpose of $a_N$ in [lem-pur-compact-support-strict-scalar-mate] is $h_N=C(\varepsilon_N)\lambda_{R_AN}$. Step 2 and the scalar comparison of Step 1 therefore identify $h_{N[r]}$ with $h_N[r]$. Under the $L_B\dashv R_B$ Hom-bijection, the shifted candidate for $a_N$ has transpose $h_N[r]$ by that same counit equation. Injectivity gives the shift square for $a$. Apply this reasoning directly on the diagram sites supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], with index category $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$. It proves equality in the derived category of strict towers using the diagram adjunction itself; no conclusion is inferred merely from equal evaluated maps.

proof.text: For the open constituent $b$ of [lem-pur-compact-support-strict-scalar-mate], extension by zero is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], so its shift comparison is termwise. In the extension-by-zero presheaf, a generator is a section $x$ in the summand indexed by an arrow $V\to X$ over $\overline X$. Both routes in the scalar/shift square send its tensor with a coefficient $b$ to the same indexed generator $x\otimes b$. These generators span the presheaf, so the maps agree before sheafification and still agree after sheafification. Both differentials on degree-shifted generators are multiplied by $(-1)^r$. The coefficient algebra is finite free and in degree zero, so the prescribed derived scalar/open maps are computed by these termwise maps. The calculation respects every diagram arrow and quotient transition, hence proves the strict diagram shift equation, rather than just its evaluations.

proof.text: By [lem-pur-compact-support-strict-scalar-mate], $q_\bullet^c$ is exactly the ordered proper/open composite on the ringed diagram sites. Whisker the open square of Step 4 by the properly derived direct image, and compose with the proper square of Step 3. The composite-shift formula and preservation under whiskering in [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker] give $s_Vq_\bullet^c(M[r])=q_\bullet^c(M)[r]s_{TU}$, with $U=\mathcal T_E^c$ and $V=(\mathcal T_F^c C_X)^{(e)}$. The source and target comparisons here are exactly those of the exact tower lifts of [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor] and of scalar extension, normalized in Step 1. Reindexing a strict complex only selects its terms and composes transitions; it does not change its differential or shift comparison. Thus this is an equality of natural transformations in the ordinary derived strict-tower category.
